lead.headline: Bitget Loses $352M in Suspected North Korean Hack as Fed Moves to Cage Stablecoins
lead.tldr: The largest exchange breach of 2025 exposes persistent custody vulnerabilities while Washington finally drafts rules for the assets everyone now wants to park in regulated wrappers. Security and policy are colliding in real time.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why it matters for the quarter ahead.

top_signals.title: Bitget CEO suspects North Korea behind $352M hack, citing IP clues
top_signals.summary: Bitget CEO Gracy Chen has indicated that North Korean hackers are likely responsible for a massive $351.6 million breach. The suspicion arises from investigators linking IP addresses used in the attack to VPN services associated with DPRK groups.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Attribution to DPRK-linked IPs raises the cost of insurance and compliance for any exchange holding user funds, particularly those with retail-heavy books that underwriters already price as higher-risk.

top_signals.title: Bitget confirms $351M security breach, suspends withdrawals7m
top_signals.summary: Bitget has confirmed a security breach resulting in a loss of $351 million. In response to the incident, the exchange has suspended all user withdrawals.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A $351 million loss with withdrawals frozen tests whether Bitget's balance sheet and any remaining insurance can absorb the hit without socializing losses, a question every LP should ask of exchange exposure.

top_signals.title: Fed proposes new capital, redemption rules for stablecoin issuers40m, Fed proposes new capital, redemption rules for stablecoin issuersThe Fed’s proposal would set capital requirements, a two-day redemption window and new reserve disclosures as regulators implement the GENIUS Act.
top_signals.summary: The Federal Reserve has proposed new regulatory requirements for stablecoin issuers, focusing on capital reserves and redemption timelines. These rules are being implemented as part of the GENIUS Act to ensure financial stability and transparency.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The GENIUS Act implementation finally gives stablecoin issuers a federal rulebook to underwrite against, but the two-day redemption window and capital requirements will compress yields and likely favor incumbents with bank relationships over crypto-native issuers.

top_signals.title: More than $170 million in crypto moves from Bitget wallets to unidentified address
top_signals.summary: Over $170 million in cryptocurrency has been moved from Bitget wallets to an unidentified address. The exchange has not yet confirmed if this movement is the result of a security breach.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $170 million pre-confirmation outflow suggests either insider coordination or monitoring failures, and either reading damages the due-diligence case for exchange custodians that claim real-time proof-of-reserves.

top_signals.title: ARK Invest brings $1.3 billion venture fund onchain through Securitize
top_signals.summary: ARK Invest has moved a $1.3 billion venture fund onchain via the Securitize platform. This move represents a significant expansion of their existing strategic partnership to leverage blockchain for asset management.
top_signals.why_it_matters: ARK's $1.3 billion onchain migration via Securitize is the largest single tokenization of venture fund interests to date, creating a live benchmark for whether LP secondaries can actually trade with institutional depth.

deals.summary: HIFI has secured $37 million in Series A funding led by Left Lane Capital. The capital will be used to scale its infrastructure for stablecoin payments and tokenized capital markets.

HIFI has raised $37 million in a Series A funding round to scale its tokenized capital markets infrastructure. The company has already established key industry ties through collaborations with DTCC and Visa.

on_the_radar.title: US weighs overseas push for dollar-backed stablecoins: Bloomberg
on_the_radar.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly exploring strategies to promote the global adoption of dollar-backed stablecoins. This move is intended to reinforce the US dollar's global dominance and increase demand for US Treasuries.

on_the_radar.title: New York moves to block Polymarket from the state, alleging it's running an illegal gambling operation
on_the_radar.summary: New York state has filed a lawsuit to block Polymarket from operating within the state, alleging the platform is running an illegal gambling operation. This move represents a significant regulatory crackdown on decentralized prediction markets.

on_the_radar.title: Ondo launches onchain portfolio tokens based on BlackRock-developed strategies
on_the_radar.summary: Ondo has launched onchain portfolio tokens that utilize investment strategies developed by BlackRock. These portfolios offer income, diversified growth, and high-growth options for eligible non-U.S. investors.

on_the_radar.title: IBM opens beta Swift ledger link for 24/7 tokenized deposits31m, IBM opens beta Swift ledger link for 24/7 tokenized depositsIBM’s beta link lets banks instruct tokenized deposit transfers on Swift’s ledger using existing payment messages and compliance processes.
on_the_radar.summary: IBM has launched a beta link allowing banks to facilitate 24/7 tokenized deposit transfers via the Swift ledger. The system integrates with existing payment messaging and compliance frameworks to streamline institutional adoption of digital assets.

on_the_radar.title: EU banking watchdog calls for crypto lending rules under MiCAThe EBA outlined potential rules for crypto lending and firms providing access to DeFi protocols as part of the European Commission’s MiCA review.
on_the_radar.summary: The European Banking Authority (EBA) has proposed new regulatory frameworks for crypto lending and DeFi access providers. These recommendations are part of the broader review of the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation.

on_the_radar.title: Block brings Bitcoin Lightning payments to x402 for AI agents
on_the_radar.summary: Block has integrated Bitcoin Lightning payments into the x402 protocol to enable financial transactions for AI agents. This move facilitates autonomous payment capabilities for AI-driven entities using the Lightning Network.

on_the_radar.title: CFTC updates guidance on tokenized assets, blockchain records after failed vote
on_the_radar.summary: The CFTC has updated its guidance regarding the use of blockchain for record-keeping and the investment of user funds into tokenized assets. These updates follow a failed vote on previous guidance released in March.

on_the_radar.title: SoFi tie-up shows stablecoins can provide alternative blockchain settlement rail
on_the_radar.summary: SoFi's integration of stablecoins demonstrates the viability of blockchain as an alternative settlement rail for financial services. The move highlights a shift toward faster, more efficient transaction processing compared to traditional banking systems.

worth_a_read.title: Exclusive: Revolut customers hit by fresh hack
worth_a_read.note: Revolut's repeat breach pattern offers a control case for whether fintechs with bank licenses actually outperform crypto-native custodians on security, or merely face quieter disclosure requirements.

worth_a_read.title: Bitcoin Consolidates While Rates Rise with Beimnet Abebe
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's rates analysis provides the macro overlay for why Bitcoin's consolidation phase may extend, directly relevant to any tokenized fund underwriting duration risk.

linkedin_post:
Gracy Chen at Bitget traced $352 million in stolen funds to North Korean VPN nodes. Withdrawals are frozen. This is the largest exchange breach this year, and it lands the same week the Fed published stablecoin redemption rules under the GENIUS Act.

The timing is not coincidence. It is pressure.

Every LP who sat through a custody pitch in the last eighteen months heard some version of proof-of-reserves, real-time monitoring, institutional-grade security. The $170 million moved from Bitget wallets before anyone confirmed a breach suggests those claims were underwriting fiction. Not necessarily malice. Just a gap between marketed controls and actual detection speed that North Korean groups have learned to exploit.

The Fed's response is to wrap stablecoin issuers in bank-like capital requirements and two-day redemption windows. That protects the onramp. It does nothing for the exchange layer where most users actually hold assets. The policy gap is obvious: regulators are pricing stablecoin risk while leaving exchange custody in a disclosure regime that lets $352 million exit before confirmation.

ARK's $1.3 billion venture fund tokenization through Securitize points to where capital is actually migrating—off exchange balance sheets and into instrument structures with clearer bankruptcy remoteness and secondary trading rails. The trade is not stablecoins versus tokenized funds. It is unwrapped exchange exposure versus anything with a legal structure and a transfer agent.

We underwrite exchange custodians on detection latency now, not marketing materials. The testable claim: any exchange that cannot confirm and contain a breach within the block confirmation window of its largest supported chain is mispriced by its users and its investors. Bitget failed that test. The repricing starts today.
